state.task: Fly through the next static gate opening in order, avoid the solid frame and ground.
state.conventions: Positive angles and rates mean LEFT or UP; negative mean RIGHT or DOWN. All directions are world motion directions, not rolled body axes. The display camera does not limit gate data.

target.geometry_note: Window gaps measure correction to ANY safe direction through the opening, not its center. Zero means current constant motion passes inside that axis. Windows move as the plane moves. No camera visibility filter.
target.interior_note: A preferred 1m extra clearance buffer, not a changed gate size or scoring rule. The original opening windows and crossing clearances remain the actual pass condition.
target.pitch_estimate_note: Opening's climb-angle window plus the currently measured nose-pitch minus flight-path-angle difference. Approximate steady-motion geometry; bank, lift, speed and lag can change this difference. No action rollout or selection.

following_transition.note: Static geometry for looking ahead; not a flight path or a required action. Pass the immediate gate first.

control.coasting_estimate_note: Approximate empirical zero-bank turn decay; no guarantee, no new action simulation. Turning and pitch affect one another.

action.instructions: Fly through every numbered gate in order. Choose pitch and bank for the next interval. Read `target.horizontal_gap_left_deg` and `target.vertical_gap_up_deg`. These signed gaps are corrections to the nearest safe edge of the gate opening. Negative horizontal gap requires RIGHT correction; positive requires LEFT. Negative vertical gap requires descent; positive requires climb. Zero gap means this motion direction already passes inside the opening. Prioritize the opening windows over the center bearing, especially immediately before crossing: center angles can grow dramatically even while the crossing is safe. When absolute horizontal gap exceeds 15 degrees, a strong bank toward the needed correction is usually appropriate. Sustain it while the gap remains large; do not reverse simply because `motion.bank_left_deg` or `measured_rates.track_turn_rate_left_deg_s` already has the desired sign. Those are evidence your turn is working, not evidence the needed correction is complete. Use `target.horizontal_gap_if_leveled_now_left_deg`, `control.estimated_extra_turn_if_leveled_left_deg` and `measured_recent_responses` to reduce bank near alignment and avoid overshoot. Keep vertical motion within `target.climb_window_up_deg`; nominal level is trim, not altitude hold. Account for measured response lag rather than reversing pitch every interval. Use `following_transition` to prepare an exit toward the following gate while still clearing the current opening. Reassess immediately when `target_update.changed_since_previous_decision` is true. Upcoming gates remain valid outside the display camera. No image is supplied. Stay within `boundary.lateral_limits_world_m`. Estimates assume unchanged motion and are approximate. Prefer the 1m interior buffer: use `target.horizontal_gap_to_interior_left_deg`, `target.vertical_gap_to_interior_up_deg` and `target.horizontal_gap_to_interior_if_leveled_left_deg` instead of correcting only after the actual opening is missed. A small gap outside the interior still needs a timely moderate correction; do not coast for several intervals until it becomes large. Aim well inside the frame, release a strong bank early enough for its remaining turn. Keep the actual opening safe when it is too late to improve the buffer. Pitch sustains vertical motion. A zero vertical gap means the CURRENT climb/descent path is safe; it does NOT mean choose level. Level targets +2 degrees nose-up and will arrest a descent or climb. Use `target.approximate_pitch_window_nose_up_deg` and the pitch target table to choose a pitch that keeps the future flight path inside the opening. The window uses current measured pitch-path difference and is approximate, particularly during a turn. Correct toward its interior early, using response history and measured path-angle rate. Maintain a suitable descent/climb pitch when motion aligns instead of alternating strong pitch and level. Account for inertia and speed. When an actual safe crossing is imminent prioritize keeping it safe over recentering. Choose bank independently using the horizontal gaps and leveling estimate. Choose one joint pitch-and-bank maneuver from the 45 choices.

criteria.up__straight: Fixed nose-up pitch target 6 degrees. Choose when this target best sustains or corrects motion toward the interior of `target.approximate_pitch_window_nose_up_deg`, accounting for actual flight-path rate, bank and measured recent responses. Negative targets sustain descent; positive targets can sustain climb. +2 trim is not a hold of current vertical velocity. Simultaneously: `target.horizontal_gap_to_interior_if_leveled_left_deg` is zero or near zero: leveling aligns with the preferred opening. Release bank toward zero degrees.
